items.definition: The flat green part of a vegetable that we eat, like cabbage or spinach.
items.example: She washed the leaves in the sink.

items.definition: The firm stem that holds leaves up. Broccoli and bok choy grow on one.
items.example: I eat the stalk of the broccoli too.

items.definition: To cook small pieces of food quickly in a little oil over a hot fire.
items.example: We stir-fry the morning glory for five minutes.

items.definition: The bowl in the bathroom where water comes out. You wash your hands and face in it.
items.example: My hands are under the sink tap.

items.definition: The small handle or knob that turns the water on and off.
items.example: Turn the tap off when you finish washing.

items.definition: The bar or liquid that makes bubbles. Bubbles carry the dirt away with the water.
items.example: There is a new bar of soap by the sink.

items.definition: A soft cloth. You use it to dry your body, your hair and your hands.
items.example: The blue towel is warm and dry.

items.definition: A small brush with bristles. You use it with toothpaste to clean your teeth.
items.example: My toothbrush is green.

items.definition: The soft thing under your head when you sleep in bed.
items.example: My pillow is soft and white.

items.definition: A thick warm cloth that covers you on cold nights.
items.example: I pull the blanket up to my chin.

items.definition: A tall cupboard with a door. You hang your clothes inside it.
items.example: My school uniform hangs in the wardrobe.

items.definition: A flat board on the wall where you keep books and other things.
items.example: There are six books on the shelf.

items.definition: A small clock that rings in the morning to wake you up.
items.example: My alarm clock rings at six.

items.definition: A bag with two straps that you carry on your back to school.
items.example: My backpack has two wide straps.

items.definition: A small bag or box that holds your pencils, pens, rubbers and ruler.
items.example: My pencil case is the blue one.

items.definition: A book of blank pages you write in at school.
items.example: I write my homework in a notebook.

items.definition: A container with a lid that holds your drink for the whole day.
items.example: I fill my water bottle at home.

items.definition: A box that carries the food you eat at the school break.
items.example: My lunch box has rice and chicken in it.

items.definition: A round shape with no corners. A wheel and a coin are circles.
items.example: The clock is a circle.

items.definition: A shape with four equal sides and four corners. A cracker is a square.
items.example: The floor tile is a square.

items.definition: A shape with three sides and three corners. A roof is a triangle.
items.example: The road sign is a triangle.

items.definition: A shape with four sides and four corners. It is longer than it is wide. A book is a rectangle.
items.example: My book is a rectangle.

items.definition: The colour of blood or fire.
One piece of content, such as a prose or gallery block.
A small toy that looks like a person. You talk for it and give it a name.
items.example: My doll is called Mai.

items.definition: A game with many pieces. You fit the pieces together to make a picture.
items.example: I finished the puzzle before dinner.

items.definition: A round toy. You throw it, catch it and kick it.
items.example: Throw me the ball, please.

items.definition: A soft toy with fur. Many children hug it or sleep with it.
items.example: My teddy bear sleeps on my pillow.

items.definition: The upward push that the wings make on a plane. It is what holds the plane in the air.
items.example: More speed means more lift on the wings.

items.definition: The forward push of a plane. The engines make the thrust.
items.example: The engines give the plane its thrust.

items.definition: The force of the air pushing back against a plane and trying to slow it down.
items.example: A smooth plane has less drag and uses less fuel.

items.definition: The pull of the Earth that pulls everything downwards, including airplanes.
items.example: Lift has to be stronger than gravity to keep the plane up.

items.definition: The shape of a wing. The curved top and flat bottom help the air push the wing up.
items.example: A good airfoil makes lift with less speed.

items.definition: Moving panels on the back edge of a wing. They make the wing bigger for take-off and landing.
items.example: The flaps come out so the plane can land slowly.

items.definition: The part under the soil. It holds the plant in place and drinks up water and minerals.
items.example: The roots reached the water at the bottom of the pot.

items.definition: The stalk of the plant. It holds the leaves up and carries water and food.
items.example: The stem was thicker this year than last year.

items.definition: The green parts that catch sunlight and make food for the plant.
items.example: The leaves turned yellow because the plant was in the dark.

items.definition: The way a leaf makes sugar from light, water and air, and gives out oxygen.
items.example: Photosynthesis is why leaves are green and why we can breathe.

items.definition: When liquid water warms up, turns into vapour, and rises into the air.
items.example: Evaporation dried the wet clothes on the line.

items.definition: When vapour cools and turns back into tiny drops of water, like the drops on a cold glass.
items.example: Condensation makes the cloud in the sky.
